voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Los Angeles, January nineteen forty-seven. Elizabeth Short, twenty-two, from Medford, Massachusetts, was found murdered in a vacant lot.
Days later, a newspaper received an envelope. Inside: her birth certificate, her photographs, her address book. Wiped with gasoline.
Then letters, signed Black Dahlia Avenger. One promised to surrender. No one came.
Police traced the names in her address book. Over the years, hundreds of people confessed. None held up.
Nearly eighty years on, no one has ever been charged with her murder.
